From 78b4d6463e9e69e5103f98b367f8984ad12cdc6f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Janusz Krzysztofik <janusz.krzysztofik@linux.intel.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Sep 2025 17:26:27 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/vgem-fence: Fix potential deadlock on release
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

A timer that expires a vgem fence automatically in 10 seconds is now
released with timer_delete_sync() from fence->ops.release() called on last
dma_fence_put().  In some scenarios, it can run in IRQ context, which is
not safe unless TIMER_IRQSAFE is used.  One potentially risky scenario was
demonstrated in Intel DRM CI trybot, BAT run on machine bat-adlp-6, while
working on new IGT subtests syncobj_timeline@stress-* as user space
replacements of some problematic test cases of a dma-fence-chain selftest
[1].

[117.004342] 6.17.0-rc7-CI_DRM_17270-g7644974e648c+ #1 Tainted: G S   U
[117.004346] 
diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
index fd76730fd38c..07db319c3d7f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ static struct dma_fence *vgem_fence_create(struct vgem_file *vfile,
 	dma_fence_init(&fence->base, &vgem_fence_ops, &fence->lock,
 		       dma_fence_context_alloc(1), 1);
 
-	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, 0);
+	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, TIMER_IRQSAFE);
 
 	/* We force the fence to expire within 10s to prevent driver hangs */
 	mod_timer(&fence->timer, jiffies + VGEM_FENCE_TIMEOUT);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

### Modifications per File

**drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c**  
- Changed `timer_setup` call from `timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, 0)` to `timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, TIMER_IRQSAFE)`.  
  This adds the `TIMER_IRQSAFE` flag to the timer.

### Relationships Between Changes

The sole modification is the addition of the `TIMER_IRQSAFE` flag to the vgem fence timer. This change is directly related to fixing a potential deadlock scenario: the fence’s release callback (`fence->ops.release`) can be invoked from IRQ context when the last `dma_fence_put()` is called, and it calls `timer_delete_sync()` to cancel the 10‑second expiration timer. Without `TIMER_IRQSAFE`, `timer_delete_sync()` is not safe to use from IRQ context (it may sleep or cause lock inversion), leading to a deadlock. By marking the timer as IRQ‑safe, the cancel operation is correctly handled in interrupt context, resolving the deadlock risk.

Here is the root cause:
The timer used for automatic fence expiration was set up without the TIMER_IRQSAFE flag. This makes it unsafe to call timer_delete_sync() from IRQ context, which can occur when the last dma_fence_put() triggers fence->ops.release() in an interrupt handler, leading to a potential deadlock.

Here is the patch:
 
 static struct dma_fence *vgem_fence_create(struct vgem_file *vfile,
 					   unsigned int flags)
 {
 	struct vgem_fence *fence;
 
 	fence = kzalloc(sizeof(*fence), GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!fence)
 		return NULL;
 
 	spin_lock_init(&fence->lock);
 	dma_fence_init(&fence->base, &vgem_fence_ops, &fence->lock,
 		       dma_fence_context_alloc(1), 1);
 
-	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, 0);
+	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, TIMER_IRQSAFE);
 
 	/* We force the fence to expire within 10s to prevent driver hangs */
 	mod_timer(&fence->timer, jiffies + VGEM_FENCE_TIMEOUT);
 
 	return &fence->base;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, 0);
timer_delete_sync(&fence->timer); // called from vgem_fence_release
```
Reason:  
`timer_setup()` is called without the `TIMER_IRQSAFE` flag, so the timer is not safe for deletion from hard IRQ context. However, `timer_delete_sync()` is invoked inside `vgem_fence_release()` (the fence’s release callback), which can be triggered by the last `dma_fence_put()` running in an interrupt handler. This creates a potential deadlock because `timer_delete_sync()` tries to acquire the timer’s internal lock, which may already be held by the running timer callback.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, TIMER_IRQSAFE);
```
Reason:  
Adding the `TIMER_IRQSAFE` flag marks the timer as safe to be deleted (or rearmed) from any context, including hard IRQ handlers. This prevents the lockdep warning and the potential deadlock described above.

MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

A timer that expires a vgem fence automatically in 10 seconds is now
released with timer_delete_sync() from fence->ops.release() called on last
dma_fence_put().  In some scenarios, it can run in IRQ context, which is
not safe unless TIMER_IRQSAFE is used.  One potentially risky scenario was
demonstrated in Intel DRM CI trybot, BAT run on machine bat-adlp-6, while
working on new IGT subtests syncobj_timeline@stress-* as user space
replacements of some problematic test cases of a dma-fence-chain selftest
[1].

Make the timer IRQ safe.

[1] https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/series/154987/#rev2

Fixes: 4077798484459 ("drm/vgem: Attach sw fences to exported vGEM dma-buf (ioctl)")
Signed-off-by: Janusz Krzysztofik <janusz.krzysztofik@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20250926152628.2165080-2-janusz.krzysztofik@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Maarten Lankhorst <dev@lankhorst.se>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
index fd76730fd38c..07db319c3d7f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/vgem/vgem_fence.c
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ static struct dma_fence *vgem_fence_create(struct vgem_file *vfile,
 	dma_fence_init(&fence->base, &vgem_fence_ops, &fence->lock,
 		       dma_fence_context_alloc(1), 1);
 
-	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, 0);
+	timer_setup(&fence->timer, vgem_fence_timeout, TIMER_IRQSAFE);
 
 	/* We force the fence to expire within 10s to prevent driver hangs */
 	mod_timer(&fence->timer, jiffies + VGEM_FENCE_TIMEOUT);
